name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Turkey's central bank raised its inflation forecast on 12 Nov; no major EM default, capital controls or IMF rescue
state: Turkey's central bank raised its end-2026 inflation forecast to 29.5% from 28% on 12 Nov, citing higher oil prices and disrupted Hormuz shipping, after annual inflation of 29.77% in October (Turkish Minute; Bloomberg, 12 Nov). The lira has weakened gradually under managed depreciation rather than falling 10% in a month. No major emerging economy had defaulted, imposed capital controls or sought emergency IMF support as of 12 Nov.
for_you: Travellers to and businesses trading with Turkey are exposed to high inflation and a weakening lira. Emerging-market borrowers in dollars are exposed to higher US rates.
rubric_hit: Normal: no major EM currency down >10% in a month, emergency IMF request, default or capital controls

sources.title: Turkish Minute — Turkey's central bank raises year-end inflation forecast to 29.5 percent
Bloomberg — Turkey raises inflation forecasts on war, fund-rout effects

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
